newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 26.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

A member of parliament of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) has been summonsed as a suspect in investigations into riots in Jakarta in July. Aberson Marle Sihaloho is the first supporter of Megawati Sukarnoputri to be called in by police.

Minister for Mines and Energy Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Wednesday that oil prices were likely to remain above US$16.50 a barrel and that 1996-97 budget forecasts are likely to be met. At the moment prices are $20.75 a barrel.

Megawati Sukarnoputri, ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), said she would defy an order from the East Jakarta mayor's office that her new party headquarters must be vacated by 6 p.m. on Thursday.

The Indonesian navy expelled 50 Chinese fishing boats with over 1,000 crew from Indonesian waters, Navy Chief-of-Staff Vice Admiral Arief Kushariadi said. The boats were illegally fishing in Indonesian waters last week, he said. They were all flying the Indonesian flag.

The capital market supervisory agency (Bapepam) is investigating a large block sale of Astra shares on Tuesday which involved a stake of around five percent in the firm. Some reports said a large share purchase was made by tobacco tycoon Putra Sampoerna.
